title: The Savoy Male and Female College
text:
Miss Maria Donovan, daughter of Cornelius and Harriet (Jones) Donovan, of Gloucester County, Virginia. Three children were born to this union. The names of the children—Hattie, Annie D., Edith B., and Connie. The professor is recognized as a gentleman of unusual experience, and his record gives good cause for such recognition as a member of the Christian Church, he has been a helpful factor in the Christian community.

One of his former students, Miss Lou Arterberry, furnishes the following information about the remainder of Professor Bohannon's service:

Mr. Bohannon was a very able instructor; one of the best the community ever had. He remained at Savoy until the College closed in 1890, when he became superintendent of schools at Bells, Texas. He taught there two years and then moved to Gainesville, where his son-in-law lived. Nothing is known after his death, which occurred in about 1895 or 1896.

Perhaps it is not insignificant to notice that his oldest daughter, Hattie Donovan Bohannon, became the author of a fairly well-known novel, "A Second Marriage: A story of Society" (G. W. Dillingham, New York, 1909), which, being a first novel, indicated a high order of literary ability. I have not found anything inferior in it written by authors of wide reputation. But after the first published novel, Miss Donovan is said to have gone South, and I have been told unable to trace her whereabouts.


PRINCIPAL AND PREPARATORY TEACHERS

Except for the references to Reverend J. H. Gay which appears earlier in this chapter, scant information has been available concerning the preparatory teachers of the Savoy College. They are such important members of the faculty, that their personalities are stamped as pleasant memories in the minds of the alumni who received their earliest and most patient training during impressionable years of childhood. The complete roll of these teachers, as far as the author has been able to compile it, includes, in the approximate order of their time of service, these teachers: Georgiana Wells White, Mr. Gay, Mr. John S.
